summary_for_children: Ad-Duha means The Morning Brightness. It comforted the Prophet (peace be upon him), reminding him of Allah's care, and teaches kindness to orphans and those who ask.
environment_concept: Bright morning light fills a meadow (93:1), while a thick grove nearby keeps the shade of the night (93:2). Further on, a home stands with its door open, a bench and a water jug outside, for kindness to the orphan and the one who asks (93:9-10). No person is shown.
architecture_and_scenery: Sunlit meadow with flowers, a dense shaded grove, a home with an open door, bench and jug.

unique_world.visual_theme: A walled bakehouse yard in a hill village on a bright morning, with a clay oven, a kneading table and a gate onto the lane

primary_mechanic.text: Knead the dough at the oven; three times a knock comes at the gate (an orphan child, a traveller, a neighbour); kneading on while someone knocks is refused, closing the gate on them is refused (93:10), and you must give what each asked (bread, water, salt); then bake.

secondary_activities: the morning brightness (93:1-5, read; the Prophet is not shown)
unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading on the lane, baking and answering the gate, then a reading under the olives
environment_behaviour: a light shows at the gate when someone knocks
the dough rises as you knead and bakes golden
unique_world.learning_objective: Do not turn away the one who asks; be kind to the orphan (93:9-10)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: A Morning Full of Hope
story_library.children_narration: Sometimes difficult moments make us feel uncertain. Surah Ad-Duha offers comfort and reassurance to Prophet Muhammad. It recalls Allah's care for him and reminds us to treat orphans and those who ask for help with kindness.

world_idea.title: The Morning of Hope
world_idea.description: Explore a beautiful sunrise environment that gradually brightens. Children learn about kindness through community-care activities.
